To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) hyperthermia and/or cisplatin treatment increase the expression of HO-1 in ovarian cancer cells, and (ii) HO-1 silencing increases the cytotoxic effect of hyperthermia and chemotherapeutic agents in gastric and ovarian cancer.

(1) HO-1 is a stress protein that can be upregulated by hyperthermia and chemotherapeutic agents; (2) HO-1 silencing in cancer cells increases their response to hyperthermic treatment; and (3) HO-1 upregulation in cancer cells may be a negative predictive factor for the response to hyperthermaic treatment.
HO-1 expression is induced by cisplatin and temperature in OVCAR3 and that HO-1 silencing increases the cytotoxic effects of cisplatin and hyperthermia in OVCAR 3 and AGS cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of HO1 expression in cancer cells and its impact on hyperthermia and chemotherapy.
the response of gastric cancer and ovarian cancer cells in vitro to hyperthermia, and the effect of prior silencing of HO-1 on the cellular response.
the response of cancer cells to hyperthermal treatment, and could be useful for the selection of patients with gastric and ovarian tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HO-1 expression is a marker of resistance of cancer cells to hyperthermal and cisplatin therapy.
the HO-1 gene is a potential target for cancer treatment.
HO-1 is not a target for the development of a new treatment strategy for gastric and ovarian cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HO-1 expression could be a predictive marker for response to hyperthermic chemotherapy in gastric and ovarian tumors.
the upregulation of Heme oxygenase-1 is associated to an inadequate response of gastric cancer cell lines to Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC) and Cisplatin.
HO-1 expression is induced by cisplatin in ovarian cancer cell line OVCAR- 3 and this upregulation is further increased by hyperthermia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HO-1 is a potential therapeutic target for hyperthermia in gastric and ovarian cancers.
the response of cancer cells to hyperthermal intraperitoneal cisplatin is dependent on HO-1 levels and that silencing of HO-1 could enhance the response to this treatment.
the induction of Heme oxygenase 1 by cisplatin is a protective mechanism for ovarian cancer cells, but this effect can be overcome by silencing Heme oxygenase-1 expression.
